newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Kabila asks UN for new mandate for rights inquiry.
newsitem.headline: Kabila asks UN for new mandate for rights inquiry.

text.p: The United Nations and the government of Congo President Laurent Kabila said on Friday they had failed to agree on the terms for a major U.N. investigation into alleged mass killings by his troops.
The joint statement, issued simultaneously in Geneva and Kinshasa after two weeks of negotiations, said the government had asked the world body to "redefine the mandate of the inquiry".

The two-page statement was signed by Emmanuel Kanbali, head of a government liaison team and Georg Mautner-Markhof, head of a small U.N. advance team which has been seeking agreement on the terms for the full inquiry due to depart on Monday.

It said that the two sides disagreed on both the composition of the team and the period the U.N. team will investigate. "As a consequence, the government of the Democratic Republic of Congo asks the United Nations to redefine the mandate of the inquiry."
"The two parties agreed to bring the results of their discussions to the attention of the U.N. Secretary-General and the U.N. Commisson on Human Rights," it added.

U.N. chief Kofi Annan indicated on Thursday he would be willing to drop Chilean lawyer Roberto Garreton, U.N. special rapporteur for Zaire, as head of mission if it could clear the way for determining the fate of missing Rwandan Hutu refugees.
